# 1\. Introduction

## 1.1 Project Overview

Our client operates the aircon service team of an aircon retailer, servicing and installing two aircon brands (M Electric and Dicon) using six vans staffed with drivers and brand-certified technicians. The client has requested a web-based workload management system that lets staff submit availability and job preferences, lets the manager visualise manpower and allocate weekly jobs, and lets IT administrators manage accounts. This report documents the requirements engineering, use case analysis, object-oriented analysis, and project management planning completed for Milestone 1\.

## 1.4 Glossary

This report uses the following capitalised terms consistently in the requirements, use cases and diagrams. The last column gives the requirement that defines or uses the term most precisely.

| Term | Meaning | Defined in |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Staff** | Field employees who receive Assignments: Drivers and Technicians. Managers are not Staff. | FR-01; §3.1 |
| **Manager** | Office-based user who records Jobs, forms Crews, allocates and publishes the Weekly Roster, and decides Staff requests. There may be several Manager accounts with the same rights. | FR-01, FR-41 |
| **IT Administrator** | User who creates accounts, changes roles, deactivates and unlocks accounts, and views the Audit Log. | FR-02, FR-04, FR-05, FR-66 |
| **Driver** | Staff member who drives a Van. The only role allowed to drive. | FR-30 |
| **Technician** | Staff member holding a Certification for one or both Brands. A Technician never drives. | FR-10, FR-30 |
| **Single-Brand Technician** | A Technician certified for only one Brand: M Electric (5 Technicians) or Dicon (4 Technicians). | FR-10; Brief, The Company, para 4 |
| **Dual-Certified Technician** | A Technician certified for both Brands (2 Technicians). One Dual-Certified Technician can cover a Van's Jobs of both Brands. | FR-10, FR-32; Brief, The Company, para 4 |
| **Brand** | Aircon brand: M Electric or Dicon. | FR-34 |
| **Certification** | A Technician's qualification for a Brand, recorded as Brand, certificate number and expiry date. It is valid for a Job when its expiry date is on or after the Job's date. | FR-10 |
| **Van** | Service vehicle, recorded by number and licence plate. The company currently has six. | FR-27 |
| **Crew** | One Driver and one or two Technicians assigned to one Van for one working day. | FR-30 |
| **Van-day** | One Van on one date, together with its Crew and Jobs. | FR-70 |
| **Job** | One Installation or Servicing task for one Brand at one address, created by the Manager. | FR-34 |
| **Job Type** | Installation or Servicing. | FR-34 |
| **Standard Duration** | The default length of a Job: 1 h per unit for Servicing and 3 h per unit for Installation. The Manager can adjust it. | FR-35 |
| **Linked Jobs** | Jobs of different Brands at the same address. They must be allocated to the same Van on the same date. | FR-36 |
| **Assignment** | A Job placed on a Van for a date. Every Crew member of that Van-day holds the Assignment. | FR-41, FR-53 |
| **Unassigned Job** | A Job with status Unassigned. Cancelled Jobs are not counted. | FR-38, FR-46 |
| **Job Allocation** | The Manager's weekly activity of creating Assignments. | FR-41 |
| **Planning Week** | A Monday-to-Saturday week. "The" Planning Week is the next unpublished one. | FR-41, FR-55 |
| **Weekly Roster** | All Crews and Assignments of one Planning Week. It is Draft until the Manager publishes it, then Published. | FR-49 |
| **Slot** | Half-day unit: Morning or Afternoon. Jobs run within 09:00–18:00 and skip lunch (13:00–14:00). | FR-13, FR-42 |
| **Availability** | A Staff member's per-Slot setting of Available or Unavailable, entered up to one month in advance. A Slot with no entry is Not submitted and counts as unavailable. | FR-13, FR-14 |
| **Availability Deadline** | 18:00 on the Wednesday 12 days before a Planning Week's Monday. After it, that week's Availability and Job Preference are locked. | FR-16 |
| **Late Availability Change Request** | A Staff request to set or change Availability for a locked week, with a reason. The Manager approves or rejects it. | FR-17 |
| **Job Preference** | A Staff member's advisory weekly preference for area, days, Slot and Job Type. A Job that breaks it raises a warning, not a block. | FR-21 |
| **Workload** | Hours credited to a Staff member: Planned Hours of Assigned Jobs plus Actual Hours of Completed Jobs, summed per Planning Week and per calendar month. | FR-53, FR-55 |
| **Travel Allowance** | A fixed 0.5 h added to each Job's hours. | FR-42, FR-53 |
| **Planned Hours / Actual Hours** | Planned Hours are a Job's duration plus the Travel Allowance. Actual Hours are the actual end minus the actual start, plus the Travel Allowance. | FR-53 |
| **Overtime** | Workload strictly above 40 h in a Planning Week. | FR-55 |
| **Job Rejection Request** | A Crew member's request to take a Job off their Van, made after a warning to discuss it with the Manager. The Manager approves or refuses it. | FR-62, FR-63 |
| **Short notice** | A Job Rejection Request submitted when the Job starts in less than 48 hours. | FR-62 |
| **Standby** | A Staff member named by the Manager to back up a working day's Jobs. Not in any Crew that day, and counted as 0 h unless placed in a Crew. | FR-71 |
| **Leave** | Annual leave in full working days: 7 per calendar year, with no carry-over. | FR-25 |
| **Leave Request** | A Staff application for Leave. The Manager approves or rejects it. | FR-22, FR-23 |
| **Workshop Servicing** | A Van's maintenance day, generated from a two-monthly rotation. The Van is unavailable that day. | FR-28 |
| **Needs attention** | A Van-day whose Crew became invalid after a later event, such as approved Leave or an expired Certification. | FR-70 |
| **Landing Page** | The first page after login, specific to each role. | FR-01 |
| **Notification** | A message to a recipient's Landing Page, with a handled state. Staff Notifications are also sent by email and phone. | FR-56, FR-64 |
| **Audit Log** | A record of who changed what and when. Only the IT Administrator can view it. | FR-66 |

2\. Requirement Engineering

## 2.1 Requirement Elicitation Process

Requirements were elicited through structured stakeholder engagement sessions using the interview guide in Appendix A, supplemented by document analysis of the client's project brief. At least five Stakeholder Representatives were engaged, covering the five stakeholder perspectives selected for the interviews: Manager, Dual-Certified Technician, Single-Brand Technician, Driver, and IT Administrator.

### 2.1.1 Elicitation Techniques Used

We combined four techniques, ordered so that each fed the next. Document analysis exposed gaps in the brief, the client settled the contradiction only it could settle, interviews and a questionnaire resolved the remaining gaps, and we then reconciled the answers into the requirements in Section 2.2.

| Technique | What we did | Why we chose it | Who was involved | Output |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Document analysis | We reviewed the client's Project Description for contradictions, undefined terms, missing processes, business rules with unclear edge cases and missing numerical or non-functional detail. For each finding we recorded the ambiguity and the interview question that would resolve it. | It costs no stakeholder time, and it makes sure interview time is spent on genuine gaps rather than on what the brief already states. | The team. | Findings table (§2.1.2) and the interview guide (Appendix A). |
| Written clarification with the client | The brief gives both "up to one month" and "up to 5 weeks" for the Availability window (F-1). We asked the lecturer, acting as the client, which applies. The lecturer confirmed one month in advance. | A contradiction inside the client's own document can only be settled by the client. A stakeholder could give an opinion, not a ruling. | The client (lecturer). | One-month Availability window (F-1; FR-14, FR-15). |
| Semi-structured interviews | We interviewed five stakeholder perspectives: Manager, Dual-Certified Technician, Single-Brand Technician, Driver and IT Administrator. Each used a role-specific guide with workflow walk-throughs, follow-up probes tied to the document-analysis findings, and scenario prompts. Sessions were run on 25/09/26 (§2.1.3). | Each role works the weekly cycle differently, and the hardest rules (valid Crews, Job rejection, late Availability changes) depend on edge cases that closed questions would miss. The IT Administrator interview supplied the performance, availability, recovery and security expectations behind the NFRs. | Five stakeholder perspectives (2.1.3). | Findings per role (§2.1.4). |
| Questionnaire (Google Form) | The updated Google Form contains 11 responses: two dual-Brand and nine single-Brand Technicians. It covers current work, Availability, Leave, preferences, Workload, request decisions, notifications and offline completion. Its response timestamps display 10/1/2026; these supersede the earlier questionnaire summary. The AI-assisted question formats were revised after a trial run (Section 1.3). | A questionnaire collects comparable answers from several respondents quickly and complements the open-ended interviews. | DB01–DB02, ME01–ME05 and DI01–DI04 (11 Technician response IDs). | Confirmed the need for clear Assignments, Manager-decided requests and planned/actual hours. Identified original/proposed Availability visibility, actionable notifications and per-Job/photo upload feedback. Reminders and extra calendar statistics remain scope questions. |

Analysis and reconciliation. Stakeholder answers did not always agree with each other or with the brief. We recorded each conflict and explained how we resolved it in Section 2.1.5. Examples:

•       The brief's "5 weeks" and "one month" Availability windows were reconciled by the client's clarification (one month).

•       The earlier interview summaries favoured immediate Job removal. The updated Technician questionnaire expects a Manager decision with clear Pending status and urgent contact when necessary. We retained the discussion warning and Manager approval, consistent with FR-62 and FR-63.

•       The IT Administrator asked both for leaver accounts to be deleted and for schedule records to be kept for a year. We resolved this by deactivating accounts and keeping their records for 12 months.

•       The Manager wanted a fixed travel allowance, while the Driver wanted estimated driving time. We adopted a fixed 0.5 h Travel Allowance per Job.

### Approximate stakeholder figures (response time, uptime, retries and so on) were turned into measurable targets and are marked in the SRS.

### 2.1.2 Document Analysis

Before conducting stakeholder interviews, the team reviewed the client's Aircon Retailer Team Project Description to extract an initial set of candidate requirements, business rules, actor roles, and ambiguities directly from the brief. The module's Team Project Overview was reviewed separately and was treated only as the source of assignment structure and stakeholder-engagement rules (e.g. milestone deadlines, the minimum of five Stakeholder Representatives, and the Week 2–6 engagement window) — it was not treated as a source of requirements for the retailer's software.

These document-analysis findings shaped the questions used in the stakeholder interview guide (Appendix A) and were subsequently checked against stakeholder answers during the engagement sessions, as summarised in Section 2.1.4.

| ID | Finding & Page Reference | Ambiguity / Missing Detail | Interview Question | Outcome / SRS Req. ID |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| F-1 | “Staff can add and edit their availabilities up to 5 weeks ahead of time.” (Aircon Retailer, Initial Requirements \#8, p.2) “employees should be able to indicate their availabilities up to one month in advance” (Overview, p.1) | Not clear whether “one month” and “five weeks” describe the same window loosely, or whether employee entry/edit, employee viewing, and manager visibility should each follow a different timeframe. | “The brief mentions both one month and five weeks. What advance period should apply to availability entry and viewing?” (Manager) | Following the lecturer’s clarification, we adopted one month in advance for Staff entry/editing and Manager viewing. We defined the window as today through the same date next month, inclusive, clamped to month end. SRS: FR-14, FR-15. |
| F-2 | “If employees miss the weekly deadline, requests would be dealt with on a case-by-case basis” (Aircon Retailer,, p.1 )  | Brief does not specify whether the system should enforce/lock the Wednesday cutoff automatically, or how a manager records and actions a case-by-case late request. | “How are availability changes submitted after Wednesday handled?” (Manager) | We agreed that Availability and Job Preference lock at 18:00 on Wednesday, 12 days before the Planning Week. Staff then request Availability changes with a reason for the Manager to approve or reject. Job Preference has no late-change route. SRS: FR-16, FR-17, FR-21. |
| F-3 | “Currently, there are six vans. Each van is made up of one driver and a qualified technician for each brand. Unless the van is servicing or installing only a particular brand, then one driver and a qualified technician for the brand. “  | Not clear whether a mixed-brand van requires two brand-specific technicians (3-person crew) or whether one dual-certified technician alone can satisfy both brands (2-person crew). | “What makes a crew valid for a day involving both aircon brands? Can one dual-certified technician and one driver cover both brands?” (Manager) | We confirmed that a Crew has exactly one Driver and 1–2 Technicians. One dual-Brand Technician can cover both Brands; otherwise one Technician per Brand is needed. Certifications must be valid for each Job. SRS: FR-30, FR-32. |
| F-4 | “On the manager’s landing page, the top three staff with the lowest workload should be shown, and highlight all staff over 40 hours of jobs allocated”; (Aircon Retailer, Initial Requirements \#6, p.2);  | No definition given for the time period the 40-hour threshold covers, what counts toward “workload” (job duration only vs. travel/waiting/other duties), or how ties for lowest workload are broken. | “What time period does the 'over 40 hours' highlight cover?” / “How should the system determine the three staff with the lowest workload?” (Manager) | We defined Workload over Monday–Saturday and Overtime as \>40 h. Every Crew member receives planned Job hours plus 0.5 h travel per Job; actual Job hours plus travel replace them on completion, excluding breaks. We adopted separate Driver/Technician rankings, excluded approved Leave in that week, and chose name A–Z for ties. SRS: FR-53, FR-55, FR-56. |
| F-5 | “Staff can reject an assigned job but “will be warned to discuss the jobs with their manager before proceeding” (Aircon Retailer, Initial Requirements \#10, p.2). | Process not specified: whether the warning is an advisory system message or a mandatory manager sign-off, and what happens to the job's status/reassignment once a rejection is confirmed. | “Walk us through what should happen when an employee rejects an assigned job.” (Manager) | We retained the discussion warning and Manager approval. The current Technician responses expect a clear Pending status and Manager decision. Pending Jobs remain Assigned. Approval makes the Job Unassigned for Manager reallocation; refusal or lapse at Job start keeps the Assignment. Less than 48 h requires an explanation and Short-notice flag. SRS: FR-62, FR-63; reallocation: FR-41, FR-50; notifications: FR-64. |

### 2.1.4 Summary of Key Findings per Stakeholder Group

We analysed the Manager, Driver and IT Administrator interview subtabs together with the updated Technician questionnaire. Its 11 response IDs are DB01–DB02, ME01–ME05 and DI01–DI04. The response timestamps display 10/1/2026; we retain that display until its date format and mapping to the attendance records are confirmed. These findings reflect the recorded answers; Section 2.1.5 distinguishes adopted refinements from open scope questions.

Manager

•       We confirmed the weekly cycle: Availability is due at 18:00 on Wednesday, planning begins on Thursday, and Monday publication covers the following Monday–Saturday. The Manager checks Vans and Availability, forms Crews before allocating Jobs, prioritises the scarce dual-certified Technicians and treats preferences as tie-breakers.

•       We found that Jobs are entered manually with customer, address, Brand, Job Type, unit count and preferred timing. Standard durations are 1 h per unit for Servicing and 3 h for Installation, with adjustments allowed. Completion needs actual times, remarks, a follow-up indicator and a signed-invoice photo.

•        We confirmed that qualification mismatches, double booking, unavailable Staff and invalid Crews must block allocation. Workload above 40 h, unmet preferences and fewer than three working Vans produce overridable warnings. The Manager also wants separate lowest-three lists for Drivers and Technicians, excluding Staff on Leave, alongside Unassigned Jobs, pending requests and Certification reminders. 

Dual-Certified Technician

•       We found that dual-Brand qualification enables mixed-Brand routes and cover duties, but does not allow simultaneous Jobs or justify durations that assume two Technicians. Before an emergency move, the Manager should check valid Certifications, Availability, existing Jobs, travel, equipment and the original Crew’s remaining Brand coverage. Respondents currently record actual Job times and send the work record to the office.

•       We identified a need to distinguish planned and actual hours, show clear Pending request outcomes and keep current Availability beside a proposed late change. The latest responses expect a Manager decision and urgent contact when a Job cannot be performed; they do not request immediate removal on submission. Notifications should identify the affected Job/date, changed timing or Crew and current details. Offline completions need per-Job/photo states, retained retry data and duplicate prevention.

Single-Brand Technician

•       We found that weekly messages, chat and urgent calls make it difficult to identify the latest Job or request outcome. Single-Brand Technicians need Brand, Job Type, units, timing, address, Crew and Linked Job information, plus clear Leave status and balance. They want current and requested Availability distinguished while Pending, with the decision visible afterwards.

•       We recorded preferences for nearby locations, sensible travel, Job Type and timing; these remain advisory. Respondents need clear Manager decisions and change messages, signed-invoice evidence and visible offline upload/photo status without losing data on failure. Devices include Android and iOS phones using Chrome, Firefox or Edge, already covered by NFR-14. Requests for reminders, extra statistics and calendar overlays remain subject to scope review.

Driver

•       We confirmed that Drivers use a phone or Van tablet to check the Job sequence, customer contact, address, time window, Brand, Job Type, Van and Crew. The Manager sets the order of Jobs. Drivers also load equipment, assist on site and wait with the Van, so they consider travel and waiting part of their working hours.

•       We identified a need for prompt updates when a Crew or Van changes, Certification-valid replacements and clear weekly/monthly hours with a 40 h warning. The Driver described five-week paper Availability entry and case-by-case late changes; this horizon was reconciled in Section 2.1.5. Approved Leave must prevent allocation, and Job rejection must include the discussion warning.

IT Administrator

•       We confirmed manual account creation, access changes restricted to the IT Administrator, company-email password recovery and audit history for account and schedule changes. The interview requested email confirmation at login and encryption of Staff and schedule data. Leaver-account deletion was reconciled with historical retention in Section 2.1.5.

•       We recorded expectations of about 50 concurrent users, responses in roughly 3–5 seconds, saved changes visible within a minute and 24/7 access, with Monday and Thursday peaks. Recovery should take no more than a day, hourly backups should limit lost updates, and schedule records should remain for a year. Browser access must work on laptops, tablets and phones.

### 2.1.5 Assumptions and Unresolved Issues

Assumptions

•       We adopted the lecturer’s one-month clarification over the conflicting five-week wording. Entry/editing and Manager viewing run from today through the same calendar date next month, inclusive, clamped to month end. Availability and Job Preference lock at 18:00 on Wednesday, 12 days before the Planning Week. (FR-14–FR-16; UC-10, UC-11.)

•       We adopted a Job-based Workload for every Crew member: Job duration plus 0.5 h Travel Allowance per Job, replaced by actual working time plus that allowance on completion; breaks are excluded. Overtime means strictly above 40 h and raises a warning. Lowest-three rankings are separate by role, exclude approved Leave and use name A–Z for ties. These adopted rules reconcile shift-based hours and route estimates. The updated Technician responses ask for the calculation to be explained; they do not independently confirm its numeric values. (FR-53, FR-55, FR-56.)

•       We retained Manager-decided Job Rejection Requests, consistent with the current Technician questionnaire. Pending Jobs stay Assigned; approval unassigns the Job and active Linked partners, while refusal or lapse at Job start retains the Assignment. There is one Pending request per shared Assignment. Short notice means less than 48 h and requires an explanation; exactly 48 h is normal. (UC-09, UC-12.)

•       We keep existing Availability while a Late Availability Change Request is Pending and update it only on approval; there is no late Job Preference route. We adopted a named Standby Staff who are Available all day and outside every Crew. Later approved Leave, Availability changes or Certification expiry can mark an existing Van-day Needs attention for Manager repair. (FR-17, FR-70, FR-71.)

•       We refined account deletion to deactivation, preserving past records for 12 months and removing future Assignments. We chose email for initial login details and SMS for the phone-notification channel. The finalized scope uses area, day, Slot and Job Type preferences; Crew-mate preferences, calendar administration and automatic replacement suggestions are outside the adopted scope. (UC-03, UC-04, UC-11, UC-15; NFR-13.)

•       We translated approximate performance and usability expectations into measurable SRS targets. Team-chosen values, including the 95% response criterion, 99% uptime, three retries and viewport/walkthrough thresholds, are identified as such in the SRS rather than attributed verbatim to interviewees. (NFR-01, NFR-05, NFR-09, NFR-14, NFR-16.)

Unresolved Issues

•       We still need the IT Administrator/team to confirm reset-link and email-confirmation-code lifetimes and password-complexity rules. Successful reset invalidates all outstanding reset tokens for that Account. (UC-01, UC-02.)

•       We need to confirm what happens to an already active session when its Account is deactivated or its role changes. (UC-04.)

•       We need to confirm whether non-status fields of a Cancelled Job can be edited. Completed and Cancelled remain final Job statuses. (UC-05.)

•       We need to define the automatic Workshop Servicing rotation for Vans added beyond the current six. Existing-Crew conflicts are already resolved by blocking that booking date. (UC-06.)

•       We need to confirm how today’s offline Assignment cache is prepared and refreshed, and how a queued completion is handled if its Job changes before upload. (UC-13, UC-14.)

•       We need the Manager/IT Administrator/team to confirm email/SMS acknowledgement and duplicate-delivery policies (UC-15). The current Technician questionnaire also raises open questions about Availability reminders, extra daily/count statistics and calendar overlays, request-history timestamps, mandatory refusal explanations and mapping exact-hour Availability to the adopted Slots. These additions are not assumed to be in scope.

## 2.2 Software Requirement Specifications

We adopted the repository’s current SRS v3.4 baseline: 50 active functional requirements and 12 active non-functional requirements. Existing IDs are retained; gaps reflect withdrawn requirements. The requirements are grouped by process area and aligned with UC-01–UC-15. A dagger (+) identifies a numeric target chosen by the team; the rationale is given below.

### 2.2.1 Functional Requirements

**Job and Weekly Roster Management**

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-34 | The Manager shall create a Job. Required: customer name, customer phone, address, postal code, Brand, Job Type (Installation or Servicing), number of units (≥1), preferred date (a working day) and preferred Slot. Optional: unit number, aircon model, notes | Must |
| FR-35 | The Job's duration shall be pre-filled from its Standard Duration (Servicing 1 h per unit, Installation 3 h per unit). The Manager can adjust it | Must |
| FR-36 | Each Job has exactly one Brand. The Manager can link Jobs of different Brands at the same address. Linked Jobs must be allocated to the same Van on the same date, and Staff see them grouped | Must |
| FR-37 | The Manager shall be able to edit or cancel a Job that is not Completed. An edited, assigned Job is re-checked against FR-44. If it now breaks a rule, it becomes Unassigned and the Manager is told why. The Crew is notified of any change or cancellation | Must |
| FR-38 | Job status shall follow these transitions only: Unassigned → Assigned (allocation). Assigned → Unassigned (an approved Job Rejection Request, Van unavailable, invalidating edit, deactivated Staff or the Manager unassigning it). While a Job Rejection Request is pending, the Job stays Assigned. Assigned → Completed (FR-39). Unassigned or Assigned → Cancelled. Completed and Cancelled are final | Must |
| FR-39 | A Technician on the Van's Crew shall mark an Assigned Job Completed. They shall record actual start and end time (end after start, both on the Job's date), a short remark, whether a follow-up visit is needed, and a required photo of the customer-signed invoice. An offline completion and its photo may be queued under NFR-08 | Must |
| FR-41 | The Manager shall allocate Jobs one Planning Week at a time (the next unpublished week), assigning each Job to a Van with a Crew on a date within that week. The allocation view shall list Staff who are available and not already in a Crew for the selected day/Slot, marking anyone named as Standby | Must |
| FR-42 | The Manager shall set each Job's start time on the Van's day. Rules: Jobs run within 09:00–18:00 and skip lunch (13:00–14:00). A Job may span both Slots. Consecutive Jobs must be at least the 0.5 h Travel Allowance apart. Jobs on the same Van must not overlap | Should |
| FR-49 | Each Planning Week's Weekly Roster shall remain Draft until the Manager publishes it. The Manager sees Draft and Published rosters; Staff see Assignments only after publication. Publishing is refused while any FR-44 violation exists and allowed with FR-45 warnings outstanding. Every Staff member with Assignments or Standby days that week is notified | Must |
| FR-50 | After publication, the Manager shall be able to add, move or unassign Jobs and change Crews for current and future dates. Changes are re-checked (FR-44 and FR-45). The removed and added Staff are notified | Must |
| FR-51 | The system shall show a weekly timeline for a selected week, with one row per Van: its Crew and Jobs, and unavailable days shaded | Must |

| FR-14 | Staff shall be able to enter or change Availability only for dates from today through the same calendar date next month, inclusive (clamped to that month's last day), and only before the Availability Deadline | Must |

Each cell shows one of five colour-coded states: available all day, morning only, afternoon only, on Leave, or unavailable / not submitted | Must |

Approval applies the change, and FR-70 applies if the change affects a Crew. Rejection leaves Availability unchanged. Staff see current Availability beside the proposed Slots and request status, with any supplied decision reason. The Staff member is notified either way | Must |

The IT Administrator enters them at account creation, and the Manager maintains them afterwards. A Certification is valid for a Job when its expiry date is on or after the Job's date | Must |
| FR-27 | The system shall store each Van's number and licence plate. The Manager maintains the Van list | Must |
| FR-28 | The system shall generate Workshop Servicing dates from the rotation: odd months Vans 1, 2 and 3; even months Vans 4, 5 and 6; on the 1st, 11th and 21st respectively. A date that falls on a Sunday moves to Monday. The Van is unavailable all that day. The Manager may adjust a generated date. If servicing needs more than one day, the Manager records the extra days as Van unavailability (FR-29) | Must |
| FR-29 | The Manager shall be able to mark a Van unavailable for a date range (e.g. breakdown). Its not-yet-completed Jobs in that range become Unassigned, its Crew for those days is released, and the Crew members are notified | Must |
| FR-30 | For each Van that is to be on service on a working day, the Manager shall form a Crew of exactly one Driver and one or two Technicians. Only Staff with the Driver role may fill the Driver position; a Technician shall never drive. Each Crew member must be available for every Slot in which the Van has Jobs. A person may be in only one Crew per day. The Crew is fixed for the day, except under FR-33 | Must |
| FR-32 | Together, a Crew's Technicians shall hold valid Certifications (FR-10) for the Brand of every Job on the Van that day. For Jobs of both Brands, this means either one dual-Brand Technician or one Technician per Brand | Must |

The Manager decides the replacement. The Van's Jobs stay on the Van until the Manager fixes the Crew. A Van becoming unavailable is handled by FR-29 | Must |
| FR-71 | For each working day of the Planning Week, the Manager shall be able to name Standby Staff from those available for the whole day and not in any Crew that day. Full cover means at least one Standby Driver, plus Standby Technicians holding valid Certifications for both Brands (one dual-Brand Technician, or one per Brand). Missing cover raises a warning (FR-45), not a block. Standby Staff back up every Job that day. They are notified when named (at publication, or immediately if the week is already Published) and when needed (FR-63, FR-70). Placing a Standby into a Crew removes them from Standby for that day. A Standby day counts 0 h of Workload unless the Standby is placed into a Crew | Should |

| FR-44 | The system shall block any allocation, Crew change, Job edit or approval that would cause: an invalid or expired Certification for a Job's Brand (FR-32); a double booking (a person in two Crews on one day, a person both in a Crew and on Standby on one day, or overlapping Jobs on a Van); a Crew member unavailable, not submitted or on Leave for a Slot the Van works; an invalid Crew (FR-30); Linked Jobs split across Vans (FR-36); a Van that is unavailable; or a Sunday | Must |
| FR-45 | The system shall warn, allow an override and log it, when an allocation or a publication would cause: a Staff member's Workload above 40 h in the Planning Week; a Job Preference not met; a Job starting outside the customer's preferred Slot; fewer than 3 Vans on service on a working day; or a working day without Standby cover (FR-71). Overtime has no approval step | Must |
| FR-46 | The system shall list the Jobs with status Unassigned and show their count. Cancelled Jobs are excluded | Must |

A Completed Job instead contributes Actual Hours equal to actual end minus actual start plus 0.5 h. Breaks are excluded; Unassigned and Cancelled Jobs contribute zero | Must |
| FR-55 | Workload is summed per Planning Week (Monday–Saturday). Workload strictly above 40 h is Overtime and is highlighted wherever Workload is shown | Must |

Before submitting, the system warns them to discuss it with the Manager first. They must pick a reason: Personal emergency; Missing equipment or parts; or Other, which requires a comment. If the Job starts less than 48 hours after submission, a written explanation is also required and the request is marked Short notice. Telling the company ahead of time that a Job can't be done uses this same function | Must |
| FR-63 | Every Job Rejection Request needs the Manager's approval, decided case by case. While it is pending, the Job stays Assigned, the Crew is still expected to do it, and the requester sees it as pending. Approved: the Job becomes Unassigned and leaves the whole Van, and the requester, the other Crew members and that day's Standby Staff are notified. Refused: the Assignment stands and the requester is notified. A request still pending when the Job starts lapses, and the Assignment stands | Must |
| FR-64 | Staff shall be notified on their Landing Page and by email and phone when: a week containing their Assignments is published; one of their Assignments is added, changed, cancelled, or removed after an approved Job Rejection Request; they are added to or removed from a Crew; they are named as Standby, or someone they back up drops out; or a decision is made on their Leave Request, Late Availability Change Request or Job Rejection Request. Each message identifies the affected Job/request and date, saved outcome, relevant changed timing/Crew, any supplied decision reason and a link to current details | Must |

| :---- | :---- | :---- |

Alert items may be marked handled | Must |
| FR-58 | The Staff Landing Page shall show: a weekly calendar of their Assignments and Standby days for the current week, switchable to the next Published week, with times, addresses and the status of any Job Rejection Request; their Workload for that week against 40 h; their Workload for the calendar month; and their Leave balance | Must |
| FR-59 | For each Assignment, Staff shall see: customer name and phone, address, unit number and postal code, Brand, model, number of units, Job Type, start time, notes, Van number and licence plate, the Crew members' names and contact numbers, and any Linked Jobs | Must |

**Accounts and Access**

| ID | Requirement Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-01 | The system shall support three roles, each with its own Landing Page: Staff (subtypes Driver and Technician), Manager and IT Administrator | Must |
| FR-02 | The IT Administrator shall create Staff and Manager accounts. Required fields: name, email, contact number and role. Technician accounts also record their Certifications (FR-10). The account starts with an initial password that the user can change | Must |
| FR-04 | The IT Administrator shall be able to change a user's role, effective from the user's next login. If a Staff member becomes a Manager, their future Assignments are removed and those Jobs become Unassigned | Must |
| FR-05 | The IT Administrator shall be able to deactivate the account of a leaver. The user can no longer log in, their future Assignments are removed (those Jobs become Unassigned), and their past records are kept | Must |
| FR-06 | A User shall be able to reset a forgotten password through a link sent to their company email. A successful reset shall atomically invalidate all outstanding password-reset tokens for that Account. | Should |
| FR-07 | An account shall lock after 5+ consecutive failed logins within 15 minutes . Only the IT Administrator can unlock it | Should |
| FR-66 | The system shall log, with who, what and when: account and role changes, password change requests, and every change to Availability, Crews, Assignments, Jobs and Leave, including overridden warnings. Only the IT Administrator can view the audit log | Should |
| FR-67 | No user may delete records dated in the past or in progress. Jobs are Cancelled rather than deleted. Future Availability entries may be cleared (FR-13) | Must |

**Prioritisation**

Must requirements cover the brief’s minimum requirements, the complete weekly workflow, blocking business rules and basic account/data protection. Should requirements are valuable stakeholder needs that do not prevent the weekly workflow from operating. The active baseline contains 45 Must and 5 Should FRs, plus 8 Must and 4 Should NFRs; no Could requirement remains in this scope.

**Reviewed use-case clarifications**

Account deactivation and Staff-to-Manager changes also remove future Crew membership and mark affected Van-days Needs attention while ending future Assignments and making their Jobs Unassigned. Role changes take effect at the next login. (UC-04; FR-04, FR-05.)

Invalidating Job edits and approved Job Rejection Requests also unassign active Linked partners. Cancellation only cancels the selected Job and unassigns its active Linked partners; Completed or already Cancelled partners remain unchanged. (UC-05, UC-09; FR-36–FR-38, FR-63.)

A Workshop Servicing booking date with an existing Crew is blocked and a warning is shown, preserving the existing Assignments. (UC-06; FR-28.)

Only one Pending Job Rejection Request is allowed per shared Assignment. Short notice means strictly less than 48 h; exactly 48 h is normal. A Job-start event lapses a request that is still Pending independently of Manager action, retains the Assignment and notifies the requester after the lapse is saved. (UC-09, UC-12; FR-62, FR-63.)

Draft roster notifications are withheld from Staff on all channels. Notifications follow a saved business event; email or SMS failure does not undo that event. The phone-notification channel is SMS. (UC-15; FR-49, FR-64.)

### 2.2.2 Non-Functional Requirements

The following requirements retain the SRS’s measurable criteria and priorities. Performance, availability, recovery, retention and device expectations come primarily from the IT Administrator interview; offline field use and usability also reflect Staff and Manager findings. Team-set criteria are marked and justified below.

| ID | Category | Requirement and Measurable Target | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-01 | Performance | With the NFR-03 load and reference dataset, 95%+ of main user actions (saving Availability, a Leave Request, an Assignment or a Job Rejection Request; loading a Landing Page) shall complete within 5 s, measured at the server. A saved change shall be visible to other logged-in users within 60 s | Should |
| NFR-03 | Capacity | The system shall support 50 concurrent sessions, including one person on up to 3devices, with a reference dataset of 6 Vans, 17 Staff, 25 Jobs per working day(above the brief's "more than 20") and 13 months of records (the 12-month retention plus the 1-month window) | Must |
| NFR-05 | Availability | The system shall be available 24/7 with ≥ 99%monthly uptime, excluding planned maintenance between 00:00 and 05:00, never on a Monday or Thursday (the peak days) | Must |
| NFR-06 | Recoverability | After a failure, service and data shall be restored within 24 h of detection, with no more than 1 h of saved data lost. Backups shall run at least hourly, and a failed backup shall alert the IT Administrator | Must |
| NFR-08 | Reliability / offline | Staff shall be able to view today's published Assignments without a connection. A Job completion (with its photo) entered offline is queued and submitted automatically when the connection returns. Each queued Job shows local/waiting, uploading, received or failed state and photo status. Details/photo are retained after failure for retry; success is confirmed only when both are received. Repeated taps or retries cannot create another completion or duplicate Workload credit | Should |
| NFR-09 | Reliability | A failed submission shall be retried automatically up to 3times. If it still fails, the user sees a message saying it was not saved and advising them to try again or contact the IT Administrator | Should |
| NFR-10 | Security | Login from a device not used in the last 30 days shall require an email confirmation (2FA), for all roles | Should |
| NFR-11 | Security | Staff personal data and schedule data shall be encrypted at rest. Passwords are stored only as salted hashes  | Must |
| NFR-12 | Security | Access shall be role-based, following the permission matrix below | Must |
| NFR-13 | Data retention | Schedule records (Jobs, Crews, Assignments, Availability, Leave) shall be kept for 12 months from their date, and may then be purged. Deactivated users' records follow the same rule | Must |
| NFR-14 | Compatibility / usability | The system shall be a browser-based web application requiring no installation. At the M2 demo it shall support the latest stable Chrome, Edge, Firefox and DuckDuckGo on Windows, Android and iOS. Staff pages shall work at 360 px width without horizontal scrolling, and Manager pages at 1366 px or wider | Must |
| NFR-16 | Usability | In a walkthrough with 3non-technical users, each shall complete "enter a week's Availability" and "submit a Job Rejection Request" without help, in under 3 minutes each | Must |

**Role-based permission matrix (NFR-12)**

Allowed \= permitted; Refused \= prohibited; own \= the User’s own records; crew \= Jobs on the Staff member’s own Van. Staff see only Published Assignments. Each prohibited role/action combination must be refused.

| Action | Driver | Technician | Manager | IT Administrator |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Set Availability, Job Preference; request Leave or a late change | own | own | Refused | Refused |
| View Assignments and Standby days | own, Published weeks only | own, Published weeks only | all | Refused |
| View Crew-mates' names and contact numbers | crew | crew | all | Refused |
| View other Staff's Availability, Leave or Workload | Refused | Refused | Allowed | Refused |
| Submit a Job Rejection Request | crew | crew | Refused | Refused |
| Mark a Job Completed | Refused | crew | Refused | Refused |
| Create, edit or cancel Jobs; form Crews; name Standby; allocate; publish | Refused | Refused | Allowed | Refused |
| Decide Leave, Late Availability Change and Job Rejection Requests | Refused | Refused | Allowed | Refused |
| Maintain Vans, Workshop Servicing dates and Certifications (after creation) | Refused | Refused | Allowed | Refused |
| Create or deactivate accounts; change roles; unlock accounts | Refused | Refused | Refused | Allowed |
| View the audit log | Refused | Refused | Refused | Allowed |

**Rationale for team-set criteria ( )**

These values are team choices recorded in the SRS, rather than stakeholder thresholds. We use them to make the requirements measurable and feasible to verify.

| ID | Team-set Criterion | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-07 | 5 failed logins in 15 min → lock | Stops password guessing while tolerating a non-technical user mistyping a few times. The IT Administrator asked for lockouts but gave no number |
| NFR-01 | 95th percentile | Response-time targets are normally stated as a percentile, so that rare network outliers don't fail an otherwise responsive system. 5 s is the upper of the IT Administrator's "3 or 5 seconds" |
| NFR-03 | Up to 3 devices per person; 25 Jobs per day; 13 months of data | The IT Administrator named multiple devices per person (phone, tablet, laptop). 25 is about 25% headroom over the brief's "more than 20 jobs … daily". 13 months \= the 12-month retention \+ the 1-month window |
| NFR-05 | ≥ 99% monthly uptime; maintenance 00:00–05:00 | 99% allows about 7 h of downtime a month, well within the IT Administrator's "Not more than one day". The window matches their "early morning or late night" and falls outside working hours (09:00–18:00) |
| NFR-09 | 3 automatic retries | Covers brief signal drops in basements without leaving the user waiting long |
| NFR-11 | Salted password hashes | Standard practice for "encrypted properly in the backend". Passwords should never be recoverable |
| NFR-14 | 360 px (Staff) / 1366 px (Manager) | 360 px is a common small Android screen width, and Technicians use their own Android phones. 1366 px is a common laptop width for the office-based Manager |
| NFR-16 | 3 users, under 3 minutes, no help | A small walkthrough is feasible for the team. The two tasks are the most frequent Staff actions, and 3 minutes is a reasonable ceiling for a weekly task |

 

# 3\. Use Cases

## 3.1 Actors

We use the actor generalisation in the approved UCD: Driver and Technician specialise Staff; Staff, Manager and IT Administrator specialise User. External actors describe email/SMS delivery and scheduled events used by the formal use cases and sequence diagrams.

| Actor | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| User (abstract) | General actor for authentication: Log In/out and Reset Password (UC-01, UC-02). Staff, Manager and IT Administrator specialise User and inherit these interactions. |
| Staff | General actor for Drivers and Technicians. Sets own Availability and Job Preference, submits Leave, Late Availability Change and Job Rejection Requests, and views own Published Assignments, Standby days, Workload and Leave balance (UC-11–UC-13). |
| Driver | Specialises Staff and is the only role permitted to drive a Van. Holds the Driver position in a Crew and uses the shared Staff use cases. A Driver cannot mark a Job Completed. |
| Technician | Specialises Staff and holds Certification for one or both Brands, covering Installation and Servicing. Uses the shared Staff use cases and may complete an Assigned Job on their Van’s Crew (UC-14). Single-Brand and dual-certified describe Certification coverage within this role. |
| Manager | Office-based User who manages Jobs, Vans and Workshop Servicing, forms Crews, names Standby, allocates and publishes Weekly Rosters, compares Staff, decides requests and views manpower information (UC-05 – UC-10). Maintains Technician Certifications after account creation. Managers are not Staff and have no own Availability, Leave or Workload. |
| IT Administrator | Creates Staff and Manager accounts, including initial Technician Certifications; changes roles, deactivates accounts, unlocks accounts and views the read-only Audit Log (UC-03, UC-04). Ongoing Certification maintenance belongs to the Manager. |
| Email Service | External actor delivering new-device confirmation, password-reset links and initial login details (UC-01 – UC-03). It also realises the email channel for Staff notifications in UC-15. |
| Email/Phone | External delivery actor shown in the UCD for system-triggered Staff notifications (UC-15). Email Service and SMS Gateway realise its email and phone channels; Staff also receive the Notification on their Landing Page. |
| SMS Gateway | External actor in the sequence analysis that realises the phone channel as SMS (UC-15). It is not a separate human role or use case. |
| Clock | Secondary system-event actor for Job-start lapse in UC-09 (SD-22) and daily Certification-expiry checks under FR-10/FR-70 (SD-16). These events run independently of a User opening a page; no separate use case is introduced. |

## 3.2 Formal Use Cases

**UC-01: Log In/out**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-01 |
| **Name** | Log In/out |
| **Primary actor** | User |
| **Secondary actors** | Email Service |
| **Description** | A User authenticates to reach the role-specific Landing Page and ends the authenticated session when finished. |
| **Trigger** | The User opens the web application or chooses Log Out. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-01, FR-07, NFR-10, NFR-12, NFR-14 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; SD-01 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The User has an active account. 2\. The web application is available in a supported browser. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens the login page and enters credentials. **System:** Validates the credentials and account status (FR-07). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Confirms the login. **System:** If the device was used within the last 30 days, creates an authenticated session (NFR-10). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** — **System:** Displays the Landing Page for the User's role (FR-01). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Chooses Log Out when finished. **System:** Ends the authenticated session and returns to the login page. |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: New or unremembered device (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system sends an email confirmation and pauses login (NFR-10). 2\. The User follows the confirmation step. 3\. The system validates the email confirmation before authenticating; a wrong or expired code creates no session. **A2: Forgotten password (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The User invokes UC-02 Reset Password. 2\. After resetting the password, the User resumes at step 1\. |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Invalid credentials or locked account (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system refuses login and records the failed attempt (FR-07). 2\. After five consecutive failures within 15 minutes, the account is locked until the IT Administrator unlocks it. **E2: Inactive account (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system refuses login without creating a session (FR-05). |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** An authenticated session exists and the correct Landing Page is displayed, or the selected session has been ended. • **Failure:** No authenticated session is created and protected data remains unavailable. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Access after login follows the SRS permission matrix (NFR-12). • Password-reset behaviour belongs to UC-02. • Logout was added by the finalized team structure. • Generic failure wording covers missing, locked, inactive and invalid-password accounts. Invalid or expired new-device confirmation creates no session. Confirmation-code lifetime is open. |
| **Open questions** | • Confirmation-code lifetime remains open. |

**UC-02: Reset Password**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-02 |
| **Name** | Reset Password |
| **Primary actor** | User |
| **Secondary actors** | Email Service |
| **Description** | A User who cannot remember the password obtains a reset link through company email and sets a new password. |
| **Trigger** | The User selects Forgot Password from UC-01. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-06, FR-66, NFR-09, NFR-11 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; SD-02 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The User has an active account with a company email address. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Enters the company email and requests a reset. **System:** Accepts the request without disclosing whether another person's account exists (FR-06). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** — **System:** Sends a reset link to the company email and logs the request (FR-06, FR-66). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Opens the link and enters a new password. **System:** Validates the link and atomically stores the new password as a salted hash (NFR-11), invalidates all outstanding reset tokens for that Account, and logs the password change (FR-66). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Returns to UC-01. **System:** Confirms the reset and allows login with the new password. |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Request is resubmitted (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The system processes the latest valid request and sends a reset email. Resubmission does not itself revoke previous links; after any successful reset, all outstanding reset tokens for that Account are invalidated. |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Link cannot be used (branches at step 3\)** 1\. The system refuses the reset and tells the User to request another link. **E2: Submission fails (branches at steps 1 or 3\)** 1\. The system retries up to three times. 2\. If saving still fails, it states that the request was not saved and advises retrying or contacting the IT Administrator (NFR-09). |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** The password is replaced and all outstanding reset tokens for the Account are unusable, and the request and password change are logged. • **Failure:** The existing password remains unchanged. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • This use case extends UC-01. Reset-token validation, the password change and invalidation of all outstanding reset tokens occur atomically. Concurrent or repeated resets recheck token validity at save time; a failed transaction preserves the prior password and token state. • Exact token lifetime and password-complexity rules are not stated in the SRS. • Reset-token lifetime and password complexity remain open; no numeric policy is assumed. |
| **Open questions** | • Confirm reset-link lifetime and password-complexity policy before implementation. Single-use behaviour is adopted. |

**UC-03: Create User Account**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-03 |
| **Name** | Create User Account |
| **Primary actor** | IT Administrator |
| **Secondary actors** | Email Service |
| **Description** | The IT Administrator creates a Staff or Manager account. |
| **Trigger** | A new Staff member or Manager needs system access. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-02, FR-10, FR-66, NFR-09, NFR-12 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; AD-04; SD-03 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The IT Administrator is logged in. 2\. The email address is not already assigned to an account. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Chooses to create an account. **System:** Displays required name, email, contact number and role fields (FR-02). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Enters the details and selects Staff subtype or Manager. **System:** Shows Certification fields when the account is for a Technician (FR-10). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Supplies required Certification details where applicable and submits. **System:** Validates required fields, email uniqueness and role authority (FR-02, NFR-12). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** — **System:** Creates the account with an initial password, logs the change and emails the initial login details to the user (FR-02, FR-66). |
| **Step 5** | **Actor:** Reviews the confirmation. **System:** Makes the account available for UC-01. |
| **Alternative flows** | None. |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Missing or duplicate data (branches at step 3\)** 1\. The system refuses the account and identifies the invalid fields (FR-02). **E2: Save fails (branches at step 4\)** 1\. The system follows the NFR-09 retry and failure-message rule. **E3: Initial-login email fails (branches at step 4\)** 1\. Warn the IT Administrator that email submission failed and offer a resend. 2\. Keep the saved account; do not create a second account to resend. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** A valid account exists with the selected role and any initial Technician Certifications. • **Failure:** No invalid account is created. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Only the IT Administrator may create accounts or assign roles (NFR-12). • Ongoing role, account-status and lockout changes belong to UC-04. • Ongoing Certification maintenance is available through UC-10 under the finalized merged structure. • If initial-login email submission fails, warn the IT Administrator and offer a resend. The saved account remains available; a channel failure does not undo creation. |
| **Open questions** | • None identified for the current draft. |

**UC-04: Manage User Access**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-04 |
| **Name** | Manage User Access |
| **Primary actor** | IT Administrator |
| **Secondary actors** | Email/Phone through UC-15 |
| **Description** | The IT Administrator changes roles, unlocks accounts, deactivates leavers and reviews the access-related audit record. |
| **Trigger** | An account's access, role or lock state requires administration. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-04, FR-05, FR-07, FR-66, NFR-12, NFR-13 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; SD-04 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The IT Administrator is logged in. 2\. The target account exists. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Searches for and selects an account. **System:** Shows its role, status and lock state. |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Selects an allowed access action and supplies any required change. **System:** Validates that the actor is an IT Administrator (NFR-12). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Confirms the change. **System:** Saves it and writes an audit entry with who, what and when (FR-66). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Reviews the result. **System:** Shows the updated account state and any affected future Assignments (FR-04, FR-05). |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Change role (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The IT Administrator selects a new role. 2\. The system applies it from the User's next login; if Staff becomes Manager, future Assignments are removed and their Jobs become Unassigned (FR-04). **A2: Deactivate a leaver (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system prevents later login, removes future Assignments, returns those Jobs to Unassigned, and retains past records (FR-05, NFR-13). **A3: Unlock an account (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system clears the FR-07 lock so the User can try UC-01 again. **A4: View audit log (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The IT Administrator opens the read-only audit log and filters or reviews entries (FR-66). |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Unauthorised actor (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system refuses the operation (NFR-12). **E2: Save fails (branches at step 3\)** 1\. The system follows the NFR-09 retry and failure-message rule. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** The selected access state is updated and audited, or the audit log is displayed. • **Failure:** The account and its Assignments remain unchanged. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Historical records are retained for 12 months from their date (NFR-13). • The finalized list merges audit-log viewing into this access-management goal. • Account deactivation and Staff-to-Manager changes atomically remove future Crew membership, flag affected Van-days Needs attention, end future Assignments, make the Jobs Unassigned and audit the changes. Notify affected Crew/eligible Standby after commit; hide Draft roster events through SD-15. |
| **Open questions** | • Confirm how active sessions behave after deactivation or a role change. |

**UC-05: Manage Job**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-05 |
| **Name** | Manage Job |
| **Primary actor** | Manager |
| **Secondary actors** | None |
| **Description** | The Manager creates, edits, links or cancels a Job while the system preserves valid status transitions and records. |
| **Trigger** | Customer work must be recorded or an existing Job must change. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-34 to FR-38, FR-44, FR-64, FR-67, NFR-09 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; SD-05 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Manager is logged in. 2\. For edit, link or cancellation, the target Job exists and is not Completed. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Chooses to create a Job. **System:** Displays required and optional Job fields (FR-34). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Enters customer, address, Brand, Job Type, unit count, preferred date and Slot. **System:** Pre-fills duration from the Standard Duration (FR-35). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Adjusts duration or optional details and submits. **System:** Validates required data, a positive unit count and a Monday–Saturday preferred date. |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** — **System:** Creates the Job as Unassigned and preserves the FR-38 status model. |
| **Step 5** | **Actor:** Reviews the saved Job. **System:** Shows it in the Unassigned Job list for UC-07 (FR-46). |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Link Jobs (branches at step 3\)** 1\. The Manager selects Jobs of different Brands at the same address. 2\. The system links them and enforces same-Van and same-date allocation (FR-36). **A2: Edit a Job (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The Manager changes a non-Completed Job. 2\. The system rechecks an Assigned Job against FR-44. 3\. A valid edit is saved; an invalidating edit returns the Job to Unassigned and states why (FR-37). **A3: Cancel a Job (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The Manager confirms cancellation of an Unassigned or Assigned Job. 2\. The system sets Cancelled, removes it from active allocation, and notifies affected Crew members through UC-15 (FR-37, FR-38, FR-64). |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Invalid or final-state change (branches at steps 3 or A2/A3)** 1\. The system refuses missing required fields, zero units, a Sunday date, or any change from Completed or Cancelled (FR-34, FR-38). **E2: Save fails** 1\. The system follows NFR-09. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** The Job is created, changed, linked or cancelled with a valid status and audit record. • **Failure:** The prior Job data and status remain unchanged. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Records dated in the past or in progress cannot be deleted; cancellation preserves the record (FR-67). • Allocation and scheduling belong to UC-07. • Link validation refuses same-Brand Jobs, different addresses or conflicting existing Van/date placements. Draft roster payloads are withheld centrally by SD-15; Published Assigned-Job changes still notify after saving. |
| **Open questions** | • Confirm whether non-status fields of a Cancelled Job remain editable. |
| **Round-3 Linked Jobs clarification** | An invalid edit that unassigns a Job also unassigns its active Linked partners. Cancellation cancels only the selected Job and unassigns active Linked partners; Completed/Cancelled partners remain unchanged. End affected placements and audit atomically, then notify eligible affected Staff after commit (FR-36/37/38). |

**UC-06: Manage Vans and Workshop Servicing**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-06 |
| **Name** | Manage Vans and Workshop Servicing |
| **Primary actor** | Manager |
| **Secondary actors** | None |
| **Description** | The Manager maintains Van records, reviews generated Workshop Servicing dates and records other Van unavailability. |
| **Trigger** | A Van is added or changed, a servicing date needs review, or a Van becomes unavailable. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-27, FR-28, FR-29, FR-38, FR-64 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; SD-06 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Manager is logged in. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens Van management. **System:** Lists Van numbers, licence plates and generated Workshop Servicing dates (FR-27, FR-28). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Selects a Van or adds a Van record. **System:** Displays editable number and licence-plate details. |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Enters or changes the details and submits. **System:** Validates and saves the Van record (FR-27). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Reviews the servicing schedule. **System:** Generates the month once using the odd/even-month rotation and moves a Sunday date to Monday (FR-28). |
| **Step 5** | **Actor:** Confirms or adjusts a generated date. **System:** Checks that no Crew exists on the proposed date, then books servicing and marks the Van unavailable all day. After a date change, frees the previous booked date only if no other unavailability reason applies. |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Record a breakdown or extra servicing days (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The Manager selects a Van and date range. 2\. The system marks the Van unavailable, releases its Crews, and makes its not-yet-completed Jobs Unassigned (FR-29). 3\. The system invokes UC-15 for released Crew members (FR-64). |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Unavailability affects completed work (branches at A1 step 2\)** 1\. The system leaves Completed Jobs unchanged (FR-29, FR-38). **E2: Save fails** 1\. The system follows NFR-09 and does not confirm unsaved changes. **E3: Workshop Servicing date has an existing Crew (branches at steps 4 or 5\)** 1\. Block that servicing date and warn the Manager; preserve the Crew and Jobs. 2\. Keep a generated conflict as an unbooked proposal. The Manager selects another date; changing a booked date is refused until a conflict-free date is supplied. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** Van data or unavailable dates are recorded; affected future Jobs and Crews follow FR-29. • **Failure:** Existing Van, Crew and Job records remain unchanged. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • The current six-Van rotation is data, while FR-27 permits additional Vans. • Reopening a generated month does not create duplicate servicing records. • Sunday is the only non-working day in the current SRS scope. • Generated-date conflicts are collected during the loop and returned once. Breakdown notifications pass through SD-15 Draft protection after the atomic business save; servicing-conflict handling remains as agreed. |
| **Open questions** | • Define automatic Workshop Servicing generation for Vans added beyond the current six. |

**UC-07: Allocate Jobs/set weekly schedule (includes forming Van Crew and publishing Weekly Roster)**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-07 |
| **Name** | Allocate Jobs/set weekly schedule (includes forming Van Crew and publishing Weekly Roster) |
| **Primary actor** | Manager |
| **Secondary actors** | Email/Phone through UC-15 |
| **Description** | The Manager prepares one Planning Week by forming daily Crews, naming Standby Staff, assigning and timing Jobs, resolving validation results and publishing the Weekly Roster. |
| **Trigger** | Planning begins for the next unpublished Planning Week or a current/future Published roster needs revision. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-30, FR-32, FR-33, FR-41 to FR-46, FR-49 to FR-51, FR-53, FR-55, FR-64, FR-71 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; AD-01; SD-17; SD-18; SD-19 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Manager is logged in. 2\. The next unpublished Planning Week exists. 3\. Jobs to allocate exist with status Unassigned. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens the Planning Week. **System:** Shows the weekly Van timeline, Unassigned Jobs, eligible Staff, Availability, Workload and existing Draft data (FR-41, FR-46, FR-51). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Selects a Van-day and chooses one Driver and one or two Technicians. **System:** Validates Crew size, roles, Availability, double booking and Certifications (FR-30 to FR-32, FR-44). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Names eligible Standby Staff for the day. **System:** Validates full-day Availability and absence from another Crew; warns when coverage is incomplete (FR-45, FR-71). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Selects an Unassigned Job, date and Van. **System:** Checks the Planning Week, Crew, Van, Linked Jobs and Brand rules (FR-41, FR-44). |
| **Step 5** | **Actor:** Sets the Job start time. **System:** Calculates its working interval, lunch interruption and travel gap; blocks overlap (FR-42). |
| **Step 6** | **Actor:** Repeats steps 2–5 until planning is complete. **System:** Recalculates Workload and displays blocking errors and overridable warnings (FR-44, FR-45). |
| **Step 7** | **Actor:** Chooses Publish. **System:** Refuses any FR-44 violation and shows outstanding FR-45 warnings. |
| **Step 8** | **Actor:** Confirms publication and any warning overrides. **System:** Changes Draft to Published and invokes UC-15 for assigned and Standby Staff (FR-49, FR-64). |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Compare Staff (branches at step 2 or 4\)** 1\. The Manager invokes UC-08 for up to three candidate Staff. 2\. On return, the Manager continues Crew formation or allocation. **A2: Change a Crew during the day (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The Manager removes and adds Staff. 2\. The system rechecks FR-30, FR-32 and FR-44 for every affected Crew, including the original Crew when a Technician is moved. It preserves completed-work credit and invokes UC-15 (FR-33, FR-64). **A3: Revise a Published roster (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The Manager adds, moves or unassigns Jobs or changes Crews for current/future dates. 2\. The system reruns validation, updates Workload and invokes UC-15 for affected Staff (FR-50). |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Blocking violation (branches at steps 2–7)** 1\. The system explains the FR-44 violation and refuses the change or publication. **E2: Warning (branches at steps 3, 6 or 7\)** 1\. The Manager may revise the schedule or override the warning. 2\. The system logs an override with who, what and when (FR-45, FR-66). **E3: Save fails** 1\. The system follows NFR-09; an unsaved roster change is not shown as complete. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** A valid Draft or Published Weekly Roster exists, with Crews, Standby and timed Assignments. • **Failure:** Invalid changes are not applied and publication state does not change. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • The Crew is fixed for a Van-day except for the FR-33 emergency change. • Past roster dates are read-only. • FR-70 is the later-event exception to FR-44; later approved Leave, approved Availability changes or Certification changes may leave an existing Crew marked Needs attention. • Validation is embedded in this merged use case rather than represented as a separate use case. |
| **Open questions** | • Resolved: FR-70 is the later-event exception to FR-44. No remaining open question in this draft. |

**UC-08: Compare Staff**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-08 |
| **Name** | Compare Staff |
| **Primary actor** | Manager |
| **Secondary actors** | None |
| **Description** | During weekly allocation, the Manager compares up to three Staff using the information needed to choose Crew members. |
| **Trigger** | The Manager requests a comparison while performing UC-07. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-43, FR-53, FR-55 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; AD-01; SD-08 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. UC-07 is active for a Job date and Planning Week. 2\. The Manager is logged in. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens Compare Staff from UC-07. **System:** Shows eligible Staff for selection. |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Selects up to three Staff. **System:** Displays each person's Availability for the day and week, Planning Week Workload, Certifications and expiry, Job Preference, and location from other Jobs (FR-43). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Reviews the side-by-side information and selects a Staff member or closes the comparison. **System:** Returns the selection to UC-07 without allocating automatically. |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Staff member has no Jobs that day (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system shows the location as “No Jobs” (FR-43). **A2: Overtime boundary is reached (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system highlights Workload only when it is strictly above 40 hours (FR-55). |

**UC-09: Manage Staff Request**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-09 |
| **Name** | Manage Staff Request |
| **Primary actor** | Manager |
| **Secondary actors** | Email/Phone through UC-15; Clock for independent Job-start lapse |
| **Description** | The Manager reviews and decides Leave, Late Availability Change and Job Rejection Requests submitted by Staff. |
| **Trigger** | A pending Staff request appears on the Manager's Landing Page, or Clock signals Job start for a Pending Job Rejection Request. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-17, FR-23 to FR-25, FR-46, FR-63, FR-64, FR-70 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; AD-03; SD-16; SD-20; SD-21; SD-22 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. For Manager decisions, the Manager is logged in. The Clock-triggered lapse does not require a Manager session. 2\. A request submitted through UC-12 is pending. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens pending requests. **System:** Lists Leave, Late Availability Change and Job Rejection Requests; Short-notice rejection requests are highlighted (FR-56). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Selects a request. **System:** Shows request details and current roster impact; late changes show current Availability beside the proposed Slots and Pending status. |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Chooses Approve or Reject/Refuse and supplies a reason where required. **System:** Validates the decision and checks affected roster rules (FR-23, FR-24, FR-44). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Confirms the decision. **System:** Applies the request-specific outcome and records the decision. |
| **Step 5** | **Actor:** — **System:** Invokes UC-15 for the requester and any other affected Staff (FR-64). |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Approve Leave (branches at step 4\)** 1\. Inside the approval save, the system rechecks the remaining balance, refuses insufficient balance, then deducts working days and marks them as Leave/Unavailable (FR-22/24/25). 2\. After warning and confirmation, apply FR-70 inside the same approval transaction; deliver returned notification events only after commit. **A2: Decide Late Availability Change (branches at step 4\)** 1\. Approval updates the requested Slots and applies FR-70 if a Crew becomes invalid. 2\. Rejection leaves Availability unchanged (FR-17). Show the decision beside the requested Slots and current Availability, including a reason when supplied. **A3: Decide Job Rejection Request (branches at step 4\)** 1\. Approval makes the Job Unassigned, removes it from the Van and updates the Unassigned count (FR-46, FR-63). 2\. Refusal leaves the Assignment in place. 3\. At Job start, the independent Clock event in SD-22 lapses a still-Pending request; the Assignment remains. Record and notify the newly saved lapse (FR-63). |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Leave rejection has no reason (branches at step 3\)** 1\. The system refuses the decision until the Manager enters a reason (FR-23). **E2: Request is no longer pending (branches at step 4\)** 1\. The system displays the current state and does not apply a second decision. **E3: Save fails** 1\. The system follows NFR-09 and leaves the request pending. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** The request has a final or lapsed status, resulting data is updated, and required notifications are issued. • **Failure:** The request remains pending and operational data is unchanged. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Staff submission belongs to UC-12; the Manager decision belongs here. • The Manager cannot directly overwrite Staff Availability. • Later events that invalidate an existing Crew follow FR-70 rather than being blocked by FR-44. • Short notice means strictly less than 48 hours; exactly 48 hours is normal. • Leave balance recheck/deduction and affected Crew changes share the approval transaction. Late Availability changes and Crew invalidation also commit together. SD-16 returns events; delivery follows commit. Clock-triggered lapse is drawn in SD-22, independent of Manager action, audited and notified after commit. |
| **Open questions** | • Exactly 48 hours remains normal. Confirm whether Late Availability rejection and Job Rejection refusal reasons become mandatory, and whether additional request-history/decision-time fields are required. Leave rejection reasons remain required by FR-23. |
| **Round-3 clarification** | Approval of a Job Rejection Request unassigns the requested Job and its active Linked partners atomically. Clock independently lapses the zero-or-one Pending request for a shared Assignment at Job start; no Manager session is required. Leave approval uses the adopted balance-serialization rule. |

**UC-11: Set Availability \+ Preferences**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-11 |
| **Name** | Set Availability \+ Preferences |
| **Primary actor** | Staff |
| **Secondary actors** | None |
| **Description** | Staff record per-Slot Availability and optional weekly Job Preference before the Availability Deadline. |
| **Trigger** | A Staff member needs to declare or revise Availability or Job Preference for an open week. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-13, FR-14, FR-16, FR-21 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; AD-02; SD-11; SD-24 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Staff member is logged in. 2\. The selected dates are between today and the same calendar date next month, inclusive. 3\. The Planning Week is not locked. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens Availability for an editable week. **System:** Shows Monday–Saturday with Morning and Afternoon Slots and the deadline (FR-13, FR-14, FR-16). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Marks each Slot Available or Unavailable, uses the whole-day shortcut, or clears an entry. **System:** Shows blank Slots as Not submitted and treats them as unavailable for allocation (FR-13). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Opens Job Preference for the same week. **System:** Shows optional area, day, Slot and Job Type fields (FR-21). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Enters any preferences and submits. **System:** Validates the date window and deadline, then saves both records. |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: No Job Preference (branches at step 3\)** 1\. The Staff member leaves every preference field blank. 2\. The system saves Availability without a preference (FR-21). |
