It offers UC-12; when the Staff member chooses requestLateChange, opens a Late Availability Change Request (FR-17). **E2: Date outside the one-month window (branches at steps 1 or 4\)** 1\. The system refuses the affected dates (FR-14). **E3: Save fails** 1\. The system follows NFR-09. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** Availability and any Job Preference are saved for the open week. • **Failure:** Prior records remain unchanged. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Job Preference is advisory; violating it creates a warning in UC-07, not a block. • Sunday Slots are not offered. • The Manager cannot directly overwrite Staff Availability. • Staff explicitly chooses to request a Late Availability Change after direct changes are refused. Setting a blank Slot creates Availability; clearing a blank Slot makes no record. Recheck the deadline at save time. |
| **Open questions** | • Confirm whether pre-deadline reminders are in scope, including timing, recipients and channels. Confirm how exact-hour Availability responses map to the adopted Morning/Afternoon Slots; the Slot model remains unchanged. |

**UC-12: Manage Requests**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-12 |
| **Name** | Manage Requests |
| **Primary actor** | Staff |
| **Secondary actors** | None |
| **Description** | Staff submit and review their Leave, Late Availability Change and Job Rejection Requests. |
| **Trigger** | A Staff member needs Leave, needs to change a locked week's Availability, or wants a Job removed from the Crew's Van. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-17, FR-22, FR-25, FR-58, FR-62 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; AD-02; AD-03; SD-23; SD-24; SD-25 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Staff member is logged in. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens Requests and selects the request type. **System:** Displays the corresponding form and current request statuses; late changes show current Availability beside proposed Slots. |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Enters the required dates, Slots, Job and/or reason. **System:** Validates request-type rules. |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Reviews the summary and submits. **System:** Creates a pending request shown on the Manager's Landing Page (FR-56). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Reviews the pending status. **System:** Keeps operational data unchanged until UC-09 decides the request. |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Submit Leave Request (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The Staff member selects full working days and may add a note. 2\. The system rejects overlap or a request exceeding the remaining seven-day annual balance (FR-22, FR-25). **A2: Submit Late Availability Change Request (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The Staff member selects one or more locked-week Slots, the new Availability and a reason. 2\. The system requires the reason and creates a Pending request (FR-17). It keeps current Availability visible beside proposed Slots and status; only approval changes Availability. After a decision, show the outcome and any supplied reason. **A3: Submit Job Rejection Request (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The Staff member selects a Job assigned to the Crew's Van in a Published week. 2\. The system warns the Staff member to discuss it with the Manager first. 3\. The Staff member selects Personal emergency, Missing equipment or parts, or Other; Other requires a comment. 4\. When the Job starts in strictly less than 48 hours, the system requires a written explanation and marks the request Short notice; exactly 48 hours is normal (FR-62). |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Required information is missing (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system identifies the missing reason, comment, explanation or date and refuses submission. **E2: Job is not eligible (branches at A3 step 1\)** 1\. Refuse a Job outside the Staff member's Crew/Published week, no longer Assigned, already started, or with another Pending request for the same Assignment (FR-62/63). **E3: Submission fails** 1\. The system follows NFR-09 and does not show a pending request unless saved. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** A valid request is pending for UC-09 and visible to the Staff member. • **Failure:** No request is created and Availability, Leave and Assignments remain unchanged. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Staff submit; the Manager decides through UC-09. • While a Job Rejection Request is pending, the Job stays Assigned (FR-63). • A second Pending Job Rejection Request for the same Assignment is refused, even from another Crew member; recheck under the atomic save. Store the less-than-48-hour Short-notice flag. Historical decided requests remain. SD-23/25 start from Staff navigation; Job-start lapse is drawn in SD-22. |
| **Open questions** | • Exactly 48 hours remains normal. Confirm whether Late Availability rejection and Job Rejection refusal reasons become mandatory, and whether additional request-history/decision-time fields are required. Leave rejection reasons remain required by FR-23. |

**UC-13: View My Assignments and Workload**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-13 |
| **Name** | View My Assignments and Workload |
| **Primary actor** | Staff |
| **Secondary actors** | None |
| **Description** | Staff view Published Assignments, Standby days, Crew and Job details, weekly and monthly Workload, request status and Leave balance. |
| **Trigger** | A Staff member opens their Landing Page or selects an Assignment. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-49, FR-53, FR-55, FR-58, FR-59, NFR-08 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; AD-01; AD-03; SD-13 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Staff member is logged in. 2\. At least the current week is available. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens the Staff Landing Page. **System:** Shows the current week's Published Assignments and Standby days, weekly Workload against 40 hours, monthly Workload and Leave balance (FR-58). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Optionally switches to the next Published week. **System:** Shows it; Draft weeks remain hidden (FR-49). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Selects an Assignment. **System:** Shows customer, address, Job, Van, Crew, contact and Linked Job details (FR-59). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Reviews Workload. **System:** Uses Planned Hours for Assigned Jobs and Actual Hours for Completed Jobs, crediting every Crew member (FR-53, FR-55). |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Offline current-day view (branches at step 1\)** 1\. With no connection, the Staff member opens cached data. 2\. The system shows today's Published Assignments (NFR-08). **A2: Job Rejection Request is pending (branches at step 3\)** 1\. The system shows the pending status while keeping the Assignment visible (FR-58, FR-63). **A3: Current week is Draft (branches at step 1\)** 1\. Show not yet published and the Leave balance, without exposing Draft Assignments (FR-49). |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Next week is Draft (branches at step 2\)** 1\. The system does not offer the Draft week to Staff (FR-49). **E2: No cached offline data (branches at A1)** 1\. The system explains that today's Assignments are unavailable offline. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** The requested read-only Assignment and Workload data is displayed. • **Failure:** No schedule or Workload data is changed. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Overtime is strictly above 40 hours per Planning Week. • Standby contributes zero Workload unless the Staff member is placed into a Crew (FR-71). • If the current week is Draft, show not yet published and the Leave balance; disclose no Draft Assignments. Published-week and cached Published-today views remain read-only. |
| **Open questions** | • Confirm how and when today’s offline cache is prepared. Also confirm whether daily totals, assigned/completed counts or Availability/Leave overlays are added; weekly/monthly Workload and Leave balance remain the adopted scope. |

**UC-14: Complete Job**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-14 |
| **Name** | Complete Job |
| **Primary actor** | Technician |
| **Secondary actors** | None |
| **Description** | A Technician on the assigned Crew records actual work details and a signed-invoice photo to complete a Job. |
| **Trigger** | Work on an Assigned Job has finished. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-38, FR-39, FR-53, NFR-08, NFR-09 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; SD-14 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. The Technician is logged in and belongs to the Job's Van Crew. 2\. The Job has status Assigned. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Opens the Assigned Job and chooses Complete. **System:** Shows actual start/end, remark, follow-up and invoice-photo fields. |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** Enters actual start and end times, a short remark and whether follow-up is needed. **System:** Validates that both times are on the Job date and end is after start (FR-39). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Attaches a photo of the customer-signed invoice. **System:** Validates that the mandatory photo is present (FR-39). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Submits completion. **System:** Rechecks Assigned state and completion authority in the atomic save. Saves details/photo together, sets Completed and calculates Actual Hours as elapsed work plus 0.5 h (FR-38, FR-39, FR-53). |
| **Step 5** | **Actor:** Reviews confirmation. **System:** Replaces Planned Hours with Actual Hours in Crew Workload. |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Complete while offline (branches at step 4\)** 1\. The system retains completion details and the invoice photo locally, showing each queued Job as local/waiting with photo status. A local save is not a server completion. 2\. When the connection returns, it shows Uploading and automatically submits through the same validation/save path (NFR-08). Confirm Received only after details and photo are saved. Failure identifies what failed and retains the item for retry without retyping or losing the photo (NFR-09). |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Actor is a Driver or outside the Crew (branches at step 1\)** 1\. The system refuses access to completion (FR-39, NFR-12). **E2: Invalid times or missing photo (branches at steps 2 or 3\)** 1\. The system identifies the error and refuses submission. **E3: Online submission fails (branches at step 4\)** 1\. The system follows NFR-09. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** The Job is Completed, evidence is stored and Workload uses Actual Hours. • **Failure:** No new completion is applied. A locally queued item is labelled awaiting upload or failed and retained for retry; the server Job remains Assigned unless another valid action changes it. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • Completed is a final Job status (FR-38). Repeated taps/retries cannot complete the Job or credit hours twice. If already Completed, show the current outcome and retain any unconfirmed queued evidence for reconciliation. • Hours remain credited to the Crew that held the completed work (FR-33). |
| **Open questions** | • Define reconciliation if the Job/Crew changes or another Technician completes the Job before a queued offline completion uploads. Do not silently overwrite or discard the retained item. |

**UC-15: Notify Staff**

| Field | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **ID** | UC-15 |
| **Name** | Notify Staff |
| **Primary actor** | Email/Phone |
| **Secondary actors** | Calling use case |
| **Description** | The system delivers required Landing Page, email and phone notifications to Staff after roster, Crew, Assignment, Standby or request-decision events. |
| **Trigger** | A calling use case commits an FR-64 or FR-71 notification event. |
| **Linked requirements** | FR-49, FR-64, FR-71, NFR-01, NFR-09 |
| **Related diagrams** | UCD-system; AD-01; AD-03; SD-15 |
| **Preconditions** | 1\. A calling use case has successfully saved a notification-triggering business event. 2\. The recipients can be identified from the saved Crew, Assignment, Standby or request data. |
| **Main flow** | **Main flow (basic path)** |
| **Step 1** | **Actor:** Calling use case supplies the event and recipients. **System:** Builds the notification from the saved event: affected Job/request and date, saved outcome, relevant changed timing/Crew, any supplied decision reason and a link to current details (FR-64). |
| **Step 2** | **Actor:** \- **System:** Adds the notification to each recipient's Landing Page (FR-64). |
| **Step 3** | **Actor:** Email/Phone accepts the outbound notification request. **System:** Generates an email and a phone notification for each recipient (FR-64). |
| **Step 4** | **Actor:** Email/Phone reports whether each delivery request was accepted. **System:** Records the result for both external channels and makes the saved change visible within 60 seconds (NFR-01). |
| **Alternative flows** | **A1: Weekly Roster publication** 1\. Notify every Staff member with Assignments or Standby days in the published week. **A2: Published roster or Crew change** 1\. Notify removed and added Staff when an Assignment or Crew changes, and notify affected Crew when a Job is changed or cancelled. **A3: Standby event** 1\. Notify Staff when named as Standby and when someone they can replace drops out (FR-71). **A4: Request decision** 1\. Notify the requester of the saved decision and reason where applicable; also notify a newly saved Job-start lapse. 2\. For an approved Job Rejection Request, also notify the other Crew members and eligible Standby Staff. **A5: Draft roster event** 1\. Withhold the Draft roster payload and recipients before creating a Landing Page message or sending email/SMS (FR-49). 2\. For mixed-week events, process Published and non-roster portions separately. |
| **Exception flows** | **E1: Email or phone delivery submission fails (branches at step 4\)** 1\. After an initial failed send, the system retries the failed email or SMS channel automatically up to three times (NFR-09). 2\. If still unsuccessful, it records the failed channel for operational follow-up and preserves the Landing Page notification. |
| **Postconditions** | • **Success:** For eligible Published/non-roster events, each intended recipient has a Landing Page notification, and email and phone notifications have been submitted. • **Failure:** The saved business event remains committed; failed delivery is visible for operational follow-up. |
| **Business rules / notes** | • The phone channel is SMS; the external actor remains Email/Phone. • SD-15 shows separate Email Service and SMS Gateway lifelines for the existing external Email/Phone actor. • UC-15 is included system behaviour; Email/Phone is its external delivery actor in the finalized list. • Callers include UC-05, UC-06, UC-07 and UC-09; other requirement-defined events may also invoke it. • SD-15 partitions events by affected week and withholds Draft roster messages on all channels; non-roster request decisions remain visible. • Notify the requester of a newly saved Job-start lapse. This resolves the earlier lapse-notification question. |
| **Open questions** | • External acknowledgement and delivery deduplication remain open, separately from preventing duplicate Job completion in UC-14. Confirm whether Late Availability rejection and Job Rejection refusal reasons become mandatory; supplied optional reasons are already delivered. |

# 4\. Object-Oriented Analysis

## 4.1 Identified Key Classes

We identified these domain classes from UC-01–UC-15 and refined their data and relationships against the current class and sequence diagrams.

| Class | Key Attributes | Key Relationships |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| User (abstract) | Name, unique email, contact number | Superclass of Staff, Manager and IT Administrator; each User owns one Account. UC-01–UC-04. |
| Staff (abstract) | Derived weekly/monthly Workload and annual Leave balance | Superclass of Driver and Technician; declares Availability and Job Preference, submits requests and views Published Assignments. Managers are not Staff. UC-11–UC-13. |
| Manager | Inherited User details | Manages Jobs, Vans, Crews, Weekly Rosters and Staff requests; compares Staff and maintains Certifications. UC-05–UC-10. |
| IT Administrator | Inherited User details | Creates Staff/Manager accounts, enters initial Certifications, manages access and views the read-only Audit Log. UC-03, UC-04. |
| Account | Salted password hash, role, active/locked state | Belongs to one User; supports login, device confirmation, password reset, role changes, deactivation and unlocking. UC-01–UC-04; NFR-11. |
| Driver | Inherited Staff details | May join one Crew per working day; the only Staff role permitted to drive a Van. UC-07, UC-13. |
| Technician | Inherited Staff details | Holds 1–2 Certifications; joins daily Crews and records completion of an Assigned Job on their Van. UC-03, UC-07, UC-10, UC-14. |
| Certification | Brand, certificate number, expiry date | Belongs to one Technician; valid when expiry is on or after the Job date. The Manager maintains it; expiry can invalidate a Crew. UC-03, UC-07, UC-10; FR-70. |
| Van | Number, licence plate, unavailable dates | Has daily Crews and Workshop Servicing records. Brand coverage comes from its Crew; other unavailability releases Crews and unassigns unfinished Jobs. UC-06, UC-07. |
| Workshop Servicing | Generated date, optional booked date | Belongs to one Van; generated from the two-monthly rotation and adjustable by the Manager. Booking a date with an existing Crew is blocked. UC-06. |
| Weekly Roster | Week start date, Draft/Published status | Contains the week’s Crews, Assignments and Standby entries; one per Planning Week. Draft Assignments remain hidden from Staff. UC-07, UC-13. |
| Crew | Date, Needs attention flag | Belongs to one Van and Weekly Roster. A valid Crew has one Driver and 1–2 Technicians. Later invalidating events permit temporary gaps marked Needs attention. UC-07, UC-09, UC-10; FR-70. |
| Assignment | Start time, current-placement flag, derived date | Links one Job to a Crew/Van-day and Weekly Roster; at most one current placement per Job. Earlier placements remain history; Completed Jobs retain their credited Staff. UC-07, UC-13, UC-14. |
| Job | Customer name/phone, address/postal code, Brand, Job Type, units, preferred date/Slot, duration and status; optional unit/model/notes; actual times, remark, follow-up flag and invoice photo | Has Assignment history. Linked Jobs have different Brands at the same address and share a Van/date. Invalidating edits and approved rejection requests also unassign active Linked partners. Cancellation cancels only the selected Job and unassigns active partners. Planned/Actual Hours include 0.5 h Travel Allowance. UC-05, UC-07, UC-09, UC-14; FR-53. |
| Standby | Date | Links one Staff member to a Weekly Roster day; Available all day, outside all Crews and credited 0 h. Joining a Crew ends that day’s Standby entry. UC-07, UC-13, UC-15. |
| Availability | Date, Slot, Available/Unavailable state | One record per Staff/date/Slot. A blank Slot is Not submitted and unavailable for allocation. Direct edits follow the one-month window and Availability Deadline. UC-11. |
| Job Preference | Week start date, optional preferred areas, days, Slot and Job Type | One advisory preference per Staff/week; shown in Staff comparison and locked with Availability. A mismatch raises a warning, not a block. UC-07, UC-08, UC-11. |
| Leave Request | Full working dates, optional note, status and rejection reason | Submitted by one Staff member; the Manager approves or rejects it. Approval deducts days from the seven-day annual balance and makes those days unavailable. UC-09, UC-12. |
| Late Availability Change Request | Requested Slot changes, reason and status | Submitted by one Staff member for a locked week. Manager approval updates Availability and handles affected Crews; it does not change Job Preference. UC-09, UC-12. |
| Job Rejection Request | Reason, comment/explanation, Short-notice flag and status | Links one requester to a shared Assignment; at most one Pending request per Assignment. Approval unassigns the Job and active Linked partners. Refusal or lapse at Job start retains the Assignment. Short notice means \<48 h. UC-09, UC-12. |
| Audit Log | Who, what and when | Records required account, password, Availability, Crew, Assignment, Job and Leave changes, including warning overrides. Only the IT Administrator may view it. UC-02–UC-07, UC-09, UC-11, UC-14; FR-66. |
| Notification | Kind, message and handled state | Has one Staff or Manager recipient. DashboardAlert supports Manager alerts; StaffMessage supports Landing Page, email and SMS delivery. Draft roster messages are withheld. UC-10, UC-15; FR-56, FR-64. |

The domain view represents business records and their relationships. Workload and annual Leave balance are derived from Assignments, Completed Jobs and approved Leave Requests; they do not require separate stored domain classes.

The boundary view represents interactions with Users, including LoginPage, LandingPage, AccountAdminPage, JobAllocationPage, RequestPage and the other use-case pages. The control view coordinates those interactions through the corresponding Controllers, RuleValidator and NotificationService. These are analysis responsibilities used by the sequence diagrams, rather than additional business entities.

Email Service, SMS Gateway and Clock are external actors. Clock drives Job-start lapse and Certification-expiry checks independently of a User opening a page. They are not domain classes.
